answer: A tide of cheap fake identities drowns open registries, so an agent economy can require each newcomer to be vouched for by a staked sponsor whose deposit is slashed if the newcomer misbehaves. A new agent starts as a small island of trust with limited spending power, earning wider access only as verified agents attest its honest work. This makes Sybil attacks expensive: an attacker posts a real bond per fake identity and risks losing it, while honest agents build a reputation lagoon of attestations no single fake can drain.
